conclusions: AIR top-p apply consumes about84us per B1 graph, versus about5.6us for the final categorical draw.
Captured torch.softmax(out=) preserves all552 sampled-state/allocation gates but increases B1 default active component time from204–206us to272–273us; production continues to use FlashInfer softmax.

AIR apply source uses one1024-thread CTA per row for the full-vocabulary retained-mass sum and normalized output pass. Parallelizing those passes is a direct implementation target; no FlashInfer source modification has been made.
limitations: The five-repeat profile includes captured reset copies between sample graphs; memcpy totals are excluded from the repeated kernel table.
Profiler kernel durations are not full-model or HTTP latency evidence.
The suggested AIR apply split requires bitwise-output and unchanged threshold/reduction validation before acceptance.
